title: Know Your Worth
summary_vi: Luyện cách trình bày và thương lượng mức lương một cách tự tin, tinh tế bằng tiếng Anh.
sentences: Most people dread the moment when an employer asks, "So, what are you looking for?"
Yet it is precisely at that point that your leverage is greatest, provided you have done your homework.
Never walk into a negotiation without a clear sense of the going rate for your role and city.
Should the first figure they offer fall short, resist the urge to accept it out of sheer relief.
Anchoring is powerful: whoever names a number first tends to shape the entire conversation that follows.
Rather than demanding more, frame your request around the value you will bring to the team.
It is not the salary alone that matters, but the whole package, including bonuses, flexibility and training budgets.
If the company genuinely cannot stretch its budget, you can still negotiate a formal review in six months.
In Hanoi and Singapore alike, hiring managers expect some back-and-forth, and a polite counteroffer rarely offends anyone.
What truly undermines candidates is not asking too much, but apologising for asking at all.
Stay composed, let silence work in your favour, and be prepared to walk away if the terms are unreasonable.
Remember that a well-handled negotiation signals precisely the confidence employers hope to see in their future colleagues.

vocabulary.example: Having a competing job offer gave her real leverage during the talks.

vocabulary.meaning_vi: mức giá/lương phổ biến hiện hành
vocabulary.example: Freelance designers in this city charge the going rate of about fifty dollars an hour.
If the proposal should fall short of our expectations, we will ask for revisions.
Anchoring explains why the first price on a menu colours how expensive the rest seems.
After a short pause, the buyer made a counteroffer that was ten percent lower.
After weeks of back-and-forth, the two firms finally signed the contract.

vocabulary.meaning_vi: rút lui, từ chối thỏa thuận
vocabulary.example: A good negotiator knows when to walk away from a deal that does not add up.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To warn candidates against changing jobs
To offer practical advice on negotiating pay
To compare salaries in different countries
questions.explanation_vi: Bài viết đưa ra lời khuyên thực tế về cách thương lượng lương.

questions.question: According to the passage, why does anchoring matter?
options: It makes employers feel more generous
It lets candidates avoid awkward silences
The first number named tends to shape the discussion
It guarantees a higher final salary
questions.explanation_vi: Người nêu con số đầu tiên thường định hướng cả cuộc trao đổi.

questions.question: What does the writer say damages a candidate's position most?
questions.explanation_vi: Tác giả cho rằng việc xin lỗi vì đã đề nghị mới là điều gây bất lợi nhất.

questions.question: What option is suggested if the budget cannot be increased?
options: Negotiating a review after six months
Asking for a longer probation period
questions.explanation_vi: Nếu ngân sách hạn chế, có thể thương lượng một cuộc xem xét lại sau sáu tháng.

title: Who Answers to the Algorithm?
summary_vi: Luyện đọc và thảo luận về các vấn đề đạo đức của trí tuệ nhân tạo với từ vựng học thuật.
sentences: Artificial intelligence is no longer a distant promise; it already decides who gets a loan, an interview or a medical scan.
That reach raises an uncomfortable question: who is accountable when an algorithm gets it wrong?
Bias is the most cited concern, and with good reason, since models learn from data that reflects historical prejudice.
A hiring tool trained on past decisions may quietly penalise women, simply because fewer of them were hired before.
Transparency offers a partial remedy, yet many systems remain black boxes even to the engineers who built them.
Were companies required to explain automated decisions, public trust would arguably be easier to earn.
Privacy poses a separate dilemma, because the data that makes these tools useful is often collected without meaningful consent.
Others worry less about present harms than about the long-term erosion of human judgement and skills.
Regulation is therefore taking shape, though lawmakers struggle to keep pace with a technology that evolves almost monthly.
In Vietnam, as elsewhere, the debate is shifting from whether to adopt AI to how to govern it responsibly.
Ultimately, it is not the machines that hold values, but the people who design, deploy and oversee them.

vocabulary.example: Managers must be held accountable for the decisions their teams make.
The study found a clear bias against older applicants.

vocabulary.meaning_vi: hệ thống "hộp đen" khó giải thích
vocabulary.example: Deep neural networks are often described as black boxes because their reasoning is hidden.

vocabulary.meaning_vi: sự đồng ý có hiểu biết thực sự
vocabulary.example: Clicking "accept" on a thirty-page policy hardly amounts to meaningful consent.
Critics fear the erosion of trust in the news media.
Schools are struggling to keep pace with the speed of technological change.

vocabulary.meaning_vi: triển khai, đưa vào sử dụng
vocabulary.example: The bank plans to deploy the new fraud-detection system next spring.

questions.question: Why does the writer say bias is a serious concern in AI?
options: Models learn from data that carries past prejudice
questions.explanation_vi: Mô hình học từ dữ liệu phản ánh định kiến trong quá khứ.

questions.question: What does the hiring-tool example illustrate?
options: A tool that is too expensive to run
Women refusing to apply for jobs
questions.explanation_vi: Ví dụ cho thấy hệ thống lặp lại sự bất công vốn có trong dữ liệu cũ.

questions.question: What is the writer's attitude towards regulation?
options: Cautiously accepting but aware of its limits
questions.explanation_vi: Tác giả ghi nhận quy định đang hình thành nhưng thừa nhận khó theo kịp công nghệ.

questions.question: What is the main message of the final sentence?
options: Companies are not responsible for software
Human beings remain responsible for AI
questions.explanation_vi: Câu cuối nhấn mạnh con người mới là bên chịu trách nhiệm về AI.

title: Concrete Meets Canopy
summary_vi: Luyện đọc bài phóng sự về thiết kế đô thị xanh với các cụm từ nâng cao về môi trường.
sentences: Walk through Singapore's Gardens by the Bay and it becomes obvious that concrete and nature need not be enemies.
Cities occupy a small fraction of the planet's land, yet they account for most of its energy consumption.
That imbalance is why planners are now rethinking streets, rooftops and even the humble pavement.
Green roofs absorb rainwater, insulate buildings and, perhaps most importantly, cool the air around them.
Cities like Copenhagen have gone further, redesigning entire districts so that heavy downpours drain into parks rather than basements.
Ho Chi Minh City, with its chronic flooding and punishing summers, has much to gain from such measures.
It is not enough, however, to plant trees and call the job done.
Without maintenance and thoughtful species selection, new greenery can wither, wasting both money and public goodwill.
Transport matters just as much; the more people cycle, walk or ride trains, the less smog settles over the skyline.
Critics warn that greening can trigger gentrification, pushing out the very residents it was meant to serve.
Addressing that risk requires affordable housing policies to be woven into the design from the outset.
A truly sustainable city, in other words, is one that is liveable for everyone, not merely photogenic.

vocabulary.example: Cars account for nearly half of the city's air pollution.
Thick walls insulate the old house against the summer heat.
Sudden downpours turned the streets into rivers within minutes.
Chronic traffic congestion costs the economy millions every year.
Without regular watering, the young saplings will wither.

vocabulary.meaning_vi: hiện tượng tầng lớp giàu đẩy giá khiến dân cũ phải rời đi
vocabulary.example: Rapid gentrification has made the old quarter unaffordable for many families.
The architect made it clear from the outset that the budget was tight.

questions.question: What contrast does the second sentence draw?
options: Small land area versus large energy use
questions.explanation_vi: Thành phố chiếm ít đất nhưng tiêu thụ phần lớn năng lượng.

questions.question: Why does the writer mention Ho Chi Minh City?
options: To show it could benefit from green measures
To compare it with Copenhagen's budget
questions.explanation_vi: Thành phố này chịu ngập và nóng nên được lợi từ các giải pháp xanh.

questions.question: What risk of greening do critics identify?
questions.explanation_vi: Các nhà phê bình lo việc làm xanh gây gentrification, đẩy dân cũ đi.

questions.question: What is implied by the last sentence?
options: Only wealthy cities can go green
questions.explanation_vi: Thành phố bền vững phải dễ sống cho mọi người, không chỉ đẹp.

title: The Mind's Shortcuts
summary_vi: Luyện đọc bài suy ngẫm về các thiên kiến nhận thức ảnh hưởng đến quyết định hằng ngày.
sentences: We like to imagine that our decisions flow from careful reasoning, but the mind prefers shortcuts.
Psychologists call these shortcuts heuristics, and while they save time, they also leave us prone to systematic error.
Take confirmation bias: once we hold a belief, we instinctively seek out evidence that supports it.
Rarely do we notice how selectively we read the news, or whom we choose to listen to.
Then there is the sunk cost fallacy, which keeps people in failing projects simply because they have already invested so much.
I once sat through an entire dreadful film for precisely that reason, having paid for the ticket.
Anchoring is subtler still, since an arbitrary first number can distort every estimate that follows.
Knowing about these traps does not make us immune; if anything, it can breed overconfidence.
What helps is slowing down, particularly when the stakes are high and emotions are running hot.
Asking a trusted friend to challenge your reasoning, or writing down your assumptions, can expose blind spots.
We will never be perfectly rational, but we can learn to catch ourselves in the act.

vocabulary.example: Tired drivers are more prone to making serious mistakes.
Confirmation bias leads us to share only the articles that agree with us.
Staying in a bad investment because of past losses is the sunk cost fallacy in action.
The deadline seemed arbitrary, since nobody could explain how it was chosen.
Constant praise can breed complacency in a young team.
Before a final exam, the stakes are high and even small errors feel enormous.

vocabulary.meaning_vi: điểm mù, thiếu sót không nhận ra
vocabulary.example: Honest feedback helps leaders identify their blind spots.

questions.question: What does the writer suggest about heuristics?
options: They save time but can mislead us
questions.explanation_vi: Heuristics tiết kiệm thời gian nhưng khiến ta dễ mắc lỗi có hệ thống.

questions.question: Why does the writer mention watching a dreadful film?
options: To illustrate a bias with a personal example
To show how little they value money
questions.explanation_vi: Đó là ví dụ cá nhân minh họa cho ngụy biện chi phí chìm.

questions.question: What ironic point is made about knowing these biases?
questions.explanation_vi: Biết về thiên kiến không giúp miễn nhiễm, thậm chí có thể gây tự tin quá mức.

questions.question: What is the tone of the final sentence?
questions.explanation_vi: Câu cuối thừa nhận sự không hoàn hảo nhưng vẫn lạc quan nhẹ nhàng.

title: Butterflies in Formation
summary_vi: Luyện nghe và nói theo một bài phát biểu về cách tự tin khi nói trước đám đông.
sentences: Good evening, everyone, and thank you for coming; I promise to keep my nerves in check.
Let me begin with a confession: for years, I would rather have done almost anything than speak in public.
My palms would sweat, my voice would tremble, and my carefully prepared words would vanish.
What changed was not that the fear disappeared, but that I learned to reinterpret it.
Those butterflies are simply your body gearing up for a challenge, and a little adrenaline sharpens focus.
Preparation matters, of course, yet over-rehearsing every word can make you sound stilted and robotic.
I now build my talks around three key ideas, which gives me something solid to fall back on.
Pausing is the most underrated skill; a well-placed silence lets your point sink in.
Equally important is eye contact, because speaking to individuals feels far less daunting than addressing a crowd.
Should you stumble, don't panic; audiences are remarkably forgiving when a speaker simply carries on.
Above all, remember that people are not there to judge you, but to hear what you have to say.
Thank you; now, I'd be glad to take your questions.

vocabulary.example: She kept her anger in check throughout the heated meeting.
The whole team is gearing up for next week's product launch.
His stilted greeting made the atmosphere even more awkward.
Having savings gave her something to fall back on when the business struggled.
It took a few days for the news of the promotion to sink in.
Starting a new career at forty can feel daunting.
Listening is an underrated skill in any leadership role.

questions.question: What kind of text is this passage most likely to be?
options: A spoken talk to an audience
questions.explanation_vi: Lời chào, cảm ơn và mời đặt câu hỏi cho thấy đây là bài nói trước khán giả.

questions.question: How did the speaker's attitude to fear change?
options: She learned to see it as useful energy
questions.explanation_vi: Cô học cách nhìn nỗi sợ như năng lượng hữu ích chứ không xóa bỏ nó.

questions.question: Why does the speaker warn against over-rehearsing?
options: It can make a talk sound unnatural
questions.explanation_vi: Tập quá kỹ từng chữ khiến bài nói nghe gượng gạo, như người máy.

questions.question: What does the speaker say about audiences?
options: They are forgiving if you carry on after a mistake
questions.explanation_vi: Khán giả khá bao dung khi diễn giả vẫn tiếp tục sau khi vấp.

title: The Price of a Glance
summary_vi: Luyện đọc bài luận về nền kinh tế chú ý và cách các nền tảng thu hút thời gian của chúng ta.
sentences: If a service is free, the old saying goes, then you are the product.
Nowhere is that truer than in the attention economy, where your time and focus are the scarce currency.
Platforms compete fiercely to hold your gaze, and they have engineered features to do precisely that.
Endless scrolling, autoplay and notification badges are not accidents; they are carefully tested to keep you coming back.
The consequences are subtle but cumulative, as fragmented attention makes sustained, deep thinking harder to achieve.
Many Vietnamese teenagers now spend hours on short videos, often without recalling what they watched.
It would be unfair, though, to cast technology as the sole villain.
These tools connect families across oceans, democratise information and give small businesses a global stage.
The real issue is design that profits from compulsion rather than genuine value.
Some users are fighting back by switching off notifications, setting screen limits or reclaiming whole evenings offline.
Regulators, meanwhile, are asking whether manipulative design should face the same scrutiny as misleading advertising.
Until incentives change, the burden will keep falling on individuals to guard their own attention.

vocabulary.example: Fresh water is becoming scarce in many coastal regions.

vocabulary.meaning_vi: được thiết kế có chủ đích
vocabulary.example: The snack was engineered to be impossible to stop eating.
The cumulative effect of poor sleep is hard to ignore.
A fragmented schedule left her no time for deep work.
Open courses aim to democratise access to higher education.
He checked his phone out of compulsion rather than need.
The company's accounts came under intense scrutiny after the scandal.

questions.question: What does "you are the product" suggest?
options: Companies profit from users' attention and data
Free services are always high quality
questions.explanation_vi: Câu nói ngụ ý công ty kiếm lời từ sự chú ý và dữ liệu của người dùng.

questions.question: According to the writer, why are features like autoplay used?
options: To keep people returning and engaged
questions.explanation_vi: Các tính năng này được thử nghiệm kỹ để giữ người dùng quay lại.

questions.question: What is the writer's overall view of technology?
options: Beneficial but flawed by manipulative design
questions.explanation_vi: Tác giả công nhận lợi ích nhưng chỉ trích thiết kế thao túng.

questions.question: What does the final sentence imply?
options: Individuals must protect their focus until incentives shift
questions.explanation_vi: Chừng nào động cơ chưa đổi, cá nhân vẫn phải tự bảo vệ sự tập trung.

title: More Than a Bowl
summary_vi: Luyện đọc bài viết về ẩm thực như một di sản văn hóa với những cách diễn đạt tinh tế.
sentences: A bowl of phở is never just a bowl of phở.
Behind its fragrant broth lies a century of migration, adaptation and fierce regional pride.
Food is among the most intimate ways a culture remembers itself, passed down not in books but in kitchens.
Grandmothers rarely measure ingredients; they rely on instinct, taste and a lifetime of repetition.
When such knowledge goes unrecorded, it can vanish within a single generation.
This is why UNESCO has begun recognising culinary traditions, from Neapolitan pizza to Korean kimchi-making, as intangible heritage.
Recognition, however, is a double-edged sword, since it may attract tourists who turn rituals into spectacle.
Street vendors in Huế, for instance, now compete with polished restaurants that serve imperial dishes in simplified form.
Purists argue that authenticity is being diluted, whereas others insist that cuisine has always evolved through borrowing.
Indeed, the bánh mì itself is a delicious product of colonial history and local ingenuity.
Perhaps the wisest approach is to document recipes faithfully while allowing cooks the freedom to improvise.
After all, a tradition that cannot breathe is merely a museum piece.

vocabulary.example: The recipe has been passed down in her family for five generations.
Folk songs are a precious form of intangible heritage.
Fame can be a double-edged sword for young chefs.
Diners often travel far in search of authenticity.

vocabulary.meaning_vi: bị pha loãng, làm yếu đi
vocabulary.example: The original message was diluted by endless compromises.
The village cooks showed great ingenuity during the food shortage.
When the shop ran out of basil, she had to improvise with mint.

questions.question: What does the opening sentence suggest about phở?
options: It is too simple to describe
questions.explanation_vi: Câu mở đầu ngụ ý phở mang nhiều ý nghĩa văn hóa hơn một món ăn.

questions.question: Why can culinary knowledge disappear so easily?
options: It is often unwritten and learned by instinct
questions.explanation_vi: Kiến thức nấu ăn thường không được ghi lại mà truyền qua trực giác.

questions.question: Why is recognition called a double-edged sword?
options: It reduces the number of tourists
It encourages cooks to leave home
It can turn traditions into spectacle
questions.explanation_vi: Sự công nhận vừa bảo vệ vừa có thể biến nghi lễ thành màn trình diễn.

questions.question: What does the writer imply with the bánh mì example?
options: Cuisine has long evolved through outside influences
questions.explanation_vi: Bánh mì cho thấy ẩm thực vốn luôn tiến hóa nhờ vay mượn.

title: Beginners Forever
summary_vi: Luyện đọc bài suy ngẫm về việc học suốt đời và cách duy trì sự tò mò khi trưởng thành.
sentences: For much of the twentieth century, education was imagined as a front-loaded affair: study first, work later.
That model is fast becoming obsolete.
Technologies shift so rapidly that skills acquired at twenty can look dated by thirty-five.
Lifelong learning, once a fashionable slogan, has therefore become a practical necessity.
Yet learning as an adult is not simply schooling repeated; it demands different habits.
Adults juggle jobs, families and fatigue, so motivation must come from relevance rather than obligation.
Many find that small, consistent effort outperforms occasional bursts of ambitious cramming.
Curiosity, moreover, is a muscle that strengthens with use and atrophies with neglect.
In Vietnam, evening classes, online courses and community libraries are widening access to people who missed formal opportunities.
Still, accessibility alone does not guarantee progress without the willingness to be a beginner again.
That humility, I would argue, is the hardest part and the most rewarding.
Those who embrace it tend to adapt more gracefully when the world inevitably changes around them.

vocabulary.meaning_vi: dồn hết vào giai đoạn đầu
vocabulary.example: The course is front-loaded, with most of the hard material in the first month.
Typewriters became obsolete once personal computers arrived.
For commuters in a big city, a motorbike is a practical necessity.

vocabulary.meaning_vi: làm tốt hơn, vượt trội hơn
vocabulary.example: Steady practice usually outperforms last-minute revision.
Cramming the night before an exam rarely leads to lasting knowledge.
A skill that is never practised slowly atrophies.
Real expertise often comes with a surprising amount of humility.

questions.question: What does the writer say about the traditional model of education?
options: It is more effective than ever
It no longer suits a fast-changing world
It should be extended to adults only
questions.explanation_vi: Mô hình học trước, làm sau đang trở nên lỗi thời.

questions.question: According to the passage, what should motivate adult learners?
questions.explanation_vi: Người lớn cần động lực đến từ sự liên quan, không phải nghĩa vụ.

questions.question: What does the metaphor of curiosity as a muscle suggest?
options: It grows through use and fades if neglected
questions.explanation_vi: Tò mò như cơ bắp: dùng thì mạnh lên, bỏ bê thì yếu đi.

questions.question: What does the writer see as the hardest part of learning?
options: Being willing to start as a beginner again
questions.explanation_vi: Tác giả cho rằng sự khiêm tốn làm người mới lại là phần khó nhất.
